name: Plinest Eye / Newest (Mastelli)

lead: Plinest Eye and Newest belong to Mastelli's range of injectable products based on highly purified polynucleotides (PN-HPT), chains of DNA fragments. Aesthetic doctors inject them into the skin to improve its quality, including texture, hydration and fine lines, with Plinest Eye aimed at the periorbital area.

A consensus report by eight experts and several randomized trials have examined PN-HPT for facial rejuvenation, nasolabial folds and acne scars, generally in small studies, and the product class is also studied for knee and tendon problems.

paras: Treatment is a clinic procedure: a practitioner injects small amounts into the skin of the target area, usually as a short series of sessions several weeks apart, sometimes followed or combined with hyaluronic acid filler. Patients describe gradual improvement in skin quality over weeks.

Injection-site reactions such as redness, swelling and bruising are the usual effects described, and as with any injectable, treatment depends on a qualified practitioner and the product's local approval status. Periocular injections need particular care.

chain: Polynucleotide product injected into the skin
Studied for effects on hydration, repair and dermal quality
Smoother, fresher-looking skin including around the eyes
angle.text: It is a clinic injectable used to improve skin quality, lines and scars. The periocular version is used on the thin skin under the eyes.

lead: Plinest Eye and Newest are injectable skin-quality products from Mastelli, an Italian company based in Sanremo, built on PN-HPT, its trademarked 'polynucleotides highly purified technology'. Polynucleotides are mixtures of DNA polymers of varying lengths, and the products are placed into the skin by clinicians to improve hydration, firmness, tone and the look of scars and fine lines.[1][2]

Plinest Eye is the periorbital product: a sterile gel containing 0.75 percent polynucleotides, labelled by the manufacturer for the delicate skin of the eye contour. Newest combines PN-HPT with linear hyaluronic acid, at 20 mg of each per 2 ml syringe, and is positioned for dehydrated and mature skin of the face, neck and decolletage.[2][3] Both are described by the company as for use by healthcare professionals in a short series of sessions.[2][3]

For someone trying to look better, the proposed chain is: intradermal injection, then hydration and tissue-repair effects described for polynucleotides, then smoother, better-textured and fresher-looking skin, including the thin skin around the eyes. Consensus guidance, randomized trials in nasolabial folds and acne scars, and a study in 30 Asian participants have examined the PN-HPT class for these outcomes.[1][4][5][6]

paras: PN-HPT products are made of purified DNA polymer mixtures. Consensus guidance describes them as part of injectable rejuvenation and revitalization approaches, used alone or in combination with other treatments.[1] An Asian-skin study describes PN-HPT, after intradermal infiltration, as promoting new collagen and extracellular matrix production.[6]

Mastelli presents itself as a family company that has specialised in polynucleotides since 1952, holding ISO 9001 and ISO 13485 quality certifications.[2] Polynucleotide and PDRN (polydeoxyribonucleotide) preparations in general are described by Wikipedia as mixtures of DNA fragments, historically isolated from human placenta in Italy and now usually purified from salmon or trout DNA.[7] The 2026 acne-scar study describes Newest as a CE-marked Class III medical device.[8]

Plinest Eye: per Mastelli, a single-use gel with polynucleotides at 0.75 percent in a 2 ml prefilled syringe, indicated for the eye contour and periorbital area, to support hydration and areas where elasticity, firmness or tone has declined, and to help reshape fibrous areas such as scars. The company describes injection into the skin with a microdroplet or retrograde linear technique, and a protocol of 3 to 4 sessions spaced 14 to 21 days apart.[2]

Newest: per Mastelli, a gel combining PN-HPT and linear hyaluronic acid with mannitol, aimed at deep hydration and skin elasticity for dehydrated and mature skin on the face, neck and decolletage, also given in 3 to 4 sessions at 14 to 21 day intervals.[3] The 2026 acne-scar cohort used Newest in sessions at baseline and weeks 2, 4 and 6.[8]

Expert consensus recommendations (agreement above 80 percent) were reached for the face, periocular area, decolletage and neck, hands, scalp and stretch marks, with details of technique, volumes and the number and spacing of sessions for each area.[1] Studies have also examined nasolabial folds and acne scars.[4][5][8]
Practitioners also use PN-HPT as a priming step before hyaluronic acid filler: the nasolabial fold study tested PN-HPT followed by cross-linked filler.[4]

Researchers describe PN-HPT as influencing cell vitality and growth, with one trial abstract describing the polynucleotide mixture as serving as an energy source for cells.[5] Wikipedia's PDRN article describes a mechanism in which breakdown of the polynucleotide releases adenosine that activates the adenosine A2A receptor, raising cAMP and increasing VEGF, together with a salvage pathway that supplies building blocks for nucleotide synthesis; lower-molecular-weight fragments are described as more active.[7] Laboratory papers describe the PN-HPT family suppressing inflammation and stimulating matrix synthesis in an osteoarthritis cell model and scavenging reactive oxygen species in hydrogels.[9][10]

Polynucleotide skin boosters sit in the injectable skin-quality category alongside hyaluronic acid boosters and biostimulators, and in appearance communities they are usually discussed in hard-maxxing contexts as clinic-delivered options for under-eye texture, fine lines and scar quality. Wikipedia says PDRN is commonly used in Asia as a skin biostimulator after procedures such as laser treatment or microneedling.[7]
A consensus report by eight experienced practitioners, published in 2021, integrated available evidence and clinical judgment into guidance for PN-HPT alone and in combination.[1]

An exploratory randomized split-face study in women aged 40 to 65 tested PN-HPT priming followed by hyaluronic acid filler for moderate to severe nasolabial folds, with saline on the other side as placebo during the priming phase.[4]

A randomized, double-blind placebo-controlled pilot of 20 women aged 30 to 50 with grade 3 to 4 atrophic acne scars compared PN-HPT with saline and assessed dermal quality with Antera 3D imaging and patient questionnaires at one and three months; the abstract reports that only the PN-HPT group improved significantly.[5] A later prospective real-world cohort of 30 women and men with the same grades used Newest and a blinded Goodman-Baron scar assessment at three and six months.[8]

A study of 30 Asian participants (mean age 40.2) gave three intradermal sessions and assessed skin tone evenness, surface evenness, firmness and glow with 3D imaging and the Global Aesthetic Improvement Scale; the abstract reports significant improvement in surface, firmness, pigmentation and radiance.[6]
Related studies examine the polynucleotide family in knee osteoarthritis and tendinitis, which are outside appearance use.[11][12][13]

The Asian-skin study abstract reports no early- or late-onset adverse events in its sample.[6] Injection-site redness, swelling and bruising are the usual effects associated with intradermal injectables. The manufacturer states the products are for healthcare professionals, and Plinest Eye is labelled specifically for the periorbital area.[2] Product availability and approval vary by country.
